newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's CTC, VTR weigh IPO for Startel.
newsitem.headline: Chile's CTC, VTR weigh IPO for Startel.

text.p: Startel, a Chilean cellular telephone venture owned jointly by Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile (CTC) and VTR, is considering an initial public stock offering, General Manager Jorge Id said Thursday.
"It is a subject which we have been studying recently," Id said at a news conference.
Id declined to give further details, stressing that the discussions were in an early stage.
Startel, which was set up last year, is Chile's largest mobile telephone company with 220,000 customers and a 59 percent market share. CTC owns 55 percent of the venture, with the rest held by VTR.
The company expects its number of customers to rise to 300,000 by December and 380,000 next year, Id said.
The increase would boost the company's market share of about 60 percent by the end of the year, he added.
CTC, 43 percent owned by Telefonica de Espana, and VTR are in talks about a possible merger of their other telecommunications operations, apart from cable television.
VTR is owned by Chile's Luksic group and SBC Communications Inc ot the United States.
